reviews.text: 挺好的战棋类爬塔游戏，可惜没多人，开放个多人模式一人控制一个英雄就更好了。 但是幽灵骷髅怪很抽象，每个英雄勇气值就3，骷髅路过碰一下就减1，没两轮就死完了。玩到进阶5，从来没在BOSS团灭过，全死在这个幽灵骷髅怪上了，这个怪平衡性非常有问题。很影响体验 打到进阶8了，我只能说这个勇气系统就是依托答辩
The demo did not accurately represent the final version. The best stuff was in the demo, and everything I paid for {in the release version) sucked.
最有交互性的RPG。每个敌人都有反击动作。数值设计堪称完美，最高难度每场战斗都是险胜，刚需操作规划承伤和出伤。4职业每个职业两个转职，共计12职业混搭，丰富度不错。下本是肉鸽爬塔，代价与收益并存。 游戏是好游戏，但玩着经常掉帧，刚打20小时打通难度9给我报错删档了，真的难绷。
Very enjoyable, if your on the fence try the demo has a seamless carry over to full game.
A hidden gem! I like the build diversity and itemization. Individual runs could be shorter. Hopefully there will be more content updates

8 hours in and most of the classes unlocked. I've done a few different runs with different compositions and completed multiple runs. This game is VERY fun if you like this genre. Some positive notes: - characters seem well balanced - parties seem well balanced - abilities and items have obvious synergies that you can build inter-character strategies around - graphics for characters and actions are good - i haven't encountered a single bug - definitely worthy of being a full release, doesn't play like an early access like many games in this genre tend to do even at full release! - skippable story if you don't care about reading it Lots to enjoy here! Satisfied customer/gamer here.

This game is great! Xcom style turn based combat with a very deep reaction system. Sometimes you can't just go all out and DPS the boss. You could inadvertently be killing one of your squishier group members. Starts out relatively easy, but the difficulty ramps up quickly. Lots to unlock with the meta progression including different classes. Reminds me of Veil of the Witch but with way deeper combat and a lot more gear and skill variety. Don't pass this up if you like turn based tactics games! And it's a frikkin steal at $15... cmon that's 1 meal. And bro you know you could do with skipping one (or 20) meals.

I've only just scratched the surface of Valor of Man so far, but I enjoyed the demo during Next Fest enough to want to pick it up on launch. It has all the hallmarks of a rouguelite game, so expect to start each run with only base abilities and gear as you pick your encounters that culminate in a boss fight at the end of each chapter. You'll get loot, gear, level ups, new abilities, upgrades, etc as you progress a run as well as unlocking more options for all of those things as you complete runs including new classes. Then you start over and do it all again. The gameplay is a grid based, tactical, and turn-based system clearly inspired by classic crpgs/ttrpgs or xcom in some ways. Enemies have their main turn action, but also will react to being attacked so you need to plan PC turns carefully. My own take on the game is it perfectly satisfies the "I want to enjoy some tactical turn-based combat" and "I don't want to do all the extra stuff in a crpg right now" feeling. I love crpgs, but sometimes I just want to fight tough monsters and get loot, then do it again. There is a story to slowly uncover, but for me this is a great standalone version of something like BG3's Trials of Tav mod. I love having a full game to fill that niche that also doesn't rely on DnD mechanics. It's easy to jump in, start a fresh run, enjoy some cool enemies and bosses, build a party, then come back later when I want to do it again. A few notes: Game is very stable and I haven't had any issues yet with bugs The devs are actively patching for balance and QoL based on player feedback Gamepad works fine, if a little clunky in particular when having to use it as a cursor to make choices It would be great to see them add UI scale or text size or something to make the game more readable when playing on a big screen (having to always zoom in on things manually isn't ideal)

If you're a fan of Slay the Spire, or tactical tun-based games, don't sleep on this one. Do yourself a fast favor, and pick it up. You can tell the developers put their hearts and souls into the making of this. They've done a helluva job. And from what i understand, it's only two people. Bought at an introductory offer price, but well worth the full price. Thanks, Team.

3.25 学习版来补票，已过征服者难度进阶10，游戏操作比较多，实际难度不大。 选路思路： 多坐火升关键技能，多打精英升等级拿遗物，一层不去商人，二三层只去抽奖商人拿饰品，看情况抽几次武器和护甲。 由于每次战斗都能补满血，而且等级和技能升级的收益很大（远大于装备和遗物），所以卷轴事件一般是不如战斗的。以及英雄负伤非常的碍事，最好不要选负伤事件。 打架思路： 绝大多数伤害能靠走位规避，所以用AP走位非常重要。 怪物存在反击机制，所以多用高伤/高暴率技能打伤害，多用远程职业/隐匿/暴击打伤害。 怪物每回合的行动卡会切换，注意有些反击卡会让怪物移动，需要适当停手等下回合再进攻。 某些怪物的aoe技能对其他怪物也有伤害（比如木乃伊/喷火恶魔/军团指挥官），有些标注了可分别敌我则没有，偶尔能用上这个机制，不过用处不大。 多段攻击会触发多次反击，非常不推荐。 aoe技能（比如闪电链）蹭到的副目标不会反击，但boss大多是单人，用处不大。 持续伤害技能的层数不会掉且不触发反击，非常的强力，打精英很顺手，即使boss有净化卡也非常好用。 能增加暴击几率或者触发隐匿/压制的技能都非常好，这是进阶难度游戏胜利的底层逻辑。 体感下来狂战士，先驱，游侠，大法师是最轮椅的阵容。战士自回扛伤，牧师加容错，游侠隐匿打弱点，法师挂点燃，没遇到过卡关的情况。选技能和装备遗物方面，如果感兴趣的人多再细说。 游戏建议： [strike]1.增加更改亮度的设置，地图界面还好，但是战斗画面太暗了。[/strike] [strike]2.增加升级获得技能的选项数，全职业解锁之后，英雄技能池变多反而构筑更困难，升级时技能二选一不太够，这时候改成三选一更合适。[/strike] [strike]3.增加混沌值的获取，打完进阶10的时候混沌值才解锁到350，感觉远远不如进阶10的难度，应该至少是550以上。[/strike] 4.创意工坊，角色画风并不美丽，也许会有高人创作更加美丽的画风（对，说的就是暗黑地牢）。 3.27 开发者的更新效率非常高！前面提到的小建议都优化了。[strike]反观某光耀夜，几个月才更新一次[/strike] 3.29 混沌1000已过，原来还有隐藏成就[strike]吓我一跳，释放混沌[/strike]。 增幅选+5暴击，+10减伤，+1勇气。挑战选负面上限+，传奇负面，践踏+3，+1mp，反击一定成功，敌人先手，无法看穿行动。 混沌选项思路： 对于0负面状态的玩法，负面上限和传奇负面就是白送的175pt。 站位分散些很少会触发践踏，也约等于白送75pt。 敌人先手，前期容错会比较低，适时让后排换抗，以及利用怪物的aoe互伤，等级高了就好了。 行动卡和反击卡都是轮完一圈才会重复，而行动卡选项比较少且一回合一次，所以保留看穿反击，也好应对反击一定成功。 低混沌没解锁后三个选项的时候可以试试升级敌人，跟打进阶10差不多。 组人还是老四样，狂战士[strike]回来吧，我的+45复苏之风，现在只有+15了[/strike]，先驱，游侠，大法师。 选人的时候角色立绘的左右箭头是可以点的，可以换初始武器和技能，二号先驱有驱散，二号游侠有+1ap和2费大弩，这两都比默认的一号角色好使。

*UPDATE*: Game is definitely much much better on PC with KB/M and enjoyed the CRPG style combat options. The UI and mouse controls allows you to get the information you need readily. Leaving the negative review as I mainly was looking for this game while traveling and for customers that are in the same boat as me. Terrible experience on the steam deck, which is where I primarily tried to play this game. I think if you played on KB/M, you probably had a much more enjoyable experience. Although it does have full controller support, it was clearly made with KB/M as priority. It takes way too many steps to even see what each enemy does, and you have to remember what the icons mean otherwise you'll forget what move the enemies are planning to do. Since there's one reaction move, and one turn action for each enemy, you have to remember 2 aspects of each enemy type on the battlefield without a quick way to get that information. I also haven't seen a fast way to see enemy ranges without scrolling over each enemy (but maybe theres a setting for this i missed) I'll try again when I have more time to use KB/M to see how the game feels there....but do not recommend if you plan to only play on steam deck

So the combat is good, it's a pretty cool tactical RPG in that regard. My issue is mainly with the replayability. I haven't really played that long, and I already feel like I've seen a good bit of what there is to see. I've encountered the same elites (mini-bosses) on multiple runs, encountered the same events multiple times. I still come across new artifacts and equipment and whatnot, but those are just a little flavoring change, not really game-changing. But more importantly, I don't feel like there's much progression. To begin with I didn't really understand what the "souls" you get at the end of each run did, the game doesn't really explain it, but I think that they are just auto-spent to unlock new content. But there's not even a bar showing, like, "200 souls to next artifact unlock," etc. A run ends and you see how many souls you got, and what you unlocked, but the number of souls feels meaningless because I have no way of quantifying their value. You unlock new classes, but those are a lateral move, they have different but not stronger options. You unlock new artifacts and gear, but you don't get those things at the start, you still encounter them randomly. You unlock new abilities, but again that just affects the pool of randomly rolled skills you can choose from when a character levels up. So I don't feel like I get stronger with each run, each run just has a few more things in the dice pool. Some things that could improve the experience: - Let me mix-and-match skills and equipment for starting builds. I have two preset choices for each class, but what if I want the weapon from one with one of the skills from another? - Give me some perks aside from unlocking things. Let me start a run with a rare rather than common weapon, or an upgraded skill, or some boosted stats, or something. I want to feel like my team is getting stronger. - Integrate the "chaos" system with the rest of the game. This could address the previous point by letting me choose some perks and some penalties for each run, although I'd also like a greater variety of perks and penalties. - Let me spend my souls! Even if it's just to unlock things for the random pool, let me spend 2000 souls on unlocking just artifacts, or spend 1000 on artifacts and 1000 on armor. Even better if I can pick which specific things to unlock. Instead of unlocking classes through story progression, make those something I can spend souls to unlock. I think my biggest problem really is that at the end of a run there are no choices other than quit or start a new run. There should be some choices between runs. I wouldn't say it's a bad game, if I could give a thumb sideways I would, but it didn't scratch the itch I was looking for personally. Each run can be fun, getting a strong build through random luck and good choices feels nice, it's just that it doesn't really feel like you're developing anything over time.

Just beat Valor 10 (the highest level). This is genuinely a great game. The general gameplay is great as it gives the illusion of reactive gameplay. In other words, when you attack, enemies respond. It reminds me of a better version of Vandal Hearts 2 (which had simultaneous movement). The weakest elements are variety and balance. There are too many build defining items which I know I can absolutely steamroll with. In other words, brute forcing can beat strategizing at that point (even in valor 10). I wish the enemies had more types of reactions. Even healing ones like 'when ally attacked, heal.' This is a great game though, especially for the price.

This is a fantastic roguelike. As others say, the way the enemies react to what you do creates a very dynamic TTRPG combat system that feels unique and requires more complex decision making than usual for this kind of combat system. There's also lots of cool gear, storyline, unlocks, etc. I'm looking forward to playing it a lot. Edit: I decided to be done with the game at this point after completing the full story. I'd like to add a little feedback for the devs: This game does some really excellent things such as the reaction system of the enemies and the critical hit system, both of which feel very fresh and unique. In fact, in general the monster design is the best part of this game. The things you fight feel very unique and challenging in different ways. The only real weakness in this game from my perspective is how our heroes grow throughout the run. The way they get stronger is very incremental and there's basically no real synergy in the game aside from characters playing roles such as tank or damage dealer. I feel this is the weakest part of the game because even though combat system itself is very engaging every run feels fairly similar. Also, the choices we get to make about how to get stronger (such as what weapon or ability to pick) usually require very little thinking. There's usually one option that's clearly better or they're both about the same value and it doesn't matter what you pick. Because there are basically no synergies and definitely no complex synergies you almost never make interesting and difficult choices about how to power up. Because of this you basically never get OP runs and the difficulty (which takes a while to come online) is very consistent which I actually like. I think if the devs could figure out a way to keep the challenge tight but offer more complex and compelling level up system the game could be a lot better and have a lot more longevity. Also many of the ways you level up or get stronger are just kind of boring and straight forward. Your characters really don't change much over the course of the run except to do what they already did just better. If the devs could mix their incredible enemy design with an equally interesting player character system I think they could make a masterpiece and I look forward to playing their next game.

已经全通进阶10了，游戏是个好游戏，但有几个地方还是美中不足，希望开发者能看得到吧。 1、难度太低，章节太少，每次队伍刚成型还没爽2把就结束了 2、感觉少了点rogue的精髓，每次重开没有任何的加点加强机制 3、每次升级2选1，随到全垃圾的时候心情很不美丽，就不能给一定的重roll的机会么？哪怕花点金币也合理啊 4、职业太少了，说是12职业，其实大部分雷同，满打满算七八个吧，而且强度明显不平衡。再就是牧师，就他一个奶妈，想给他整点花活都不行，限定死了。 5、弓弩没有存在感，双倍的费用只比1费伤害高一点点，能整个1费连弩职业不。 6、怪物的无限反击机制决定了压制、扰乱、暴击的绝对优势，其它技能不值一提。 7、前面章节的商店不知道存在的意义在哪，收益极低，不行你删了它吧。 8、有些中文翻译不敢恭维，开始玩的时候纯靠猜。

8/10 Perfect for Tactical Turn-Based Fans I love the turn based Action Point system here. As someone who’s a big fan of Pathfinder 2.0’s 3 action economy, I’ve always been disappointed that Owlcat never leaned into that style again. Valor of Man really fills that void, at least from a tactical combat perspective. You’ve got a party of 4 characters, each with around 3 subclasses, and they all feel distinct with clear roles. The combat is where the game shines. It’s flexible, thoughtful, and rewards planning without feeling overly punishing. The story has a really cool hook too. Humanity is stuck in a never ending loop, and your character slowly starts remembering past cycles. Each time you beat the third boss, things reset but not quite the same. Dialogues start familiar but end differently, and characters can shift into entirely different versions of themselves. It’s a great idea. That said, the execution doesn’t fully land. The writing can feel a bit too brief, and it seems like translation issues get in the way at times. As the loops go on, the changes become harder to follow instead of more intriguing. It also doesn’t help that the game reuses the same handful of background art pieces, which makes everything blur together after a while. Still, if you’re here for tactical combat and that Pathfinder style action economy, this absolutely delivers. It’s not perfect, but it scratches a very specific itch that not many games even try to reach.

还不错的肉鸽战旗。 不过问题也不少。 1.肉鸽最重要的重玩价值不高，打下来感觉每把都大同小异，没什么大幅度的流派变化 2.机制决定了暴击高于一切，不过玩什么都看到暴击拿暴击了 3。升级带来的期待值也不高，没什么特别有趣的套路变化。 4，有些技能有点太抽象了，狂战士自回15%血不像人设计的，即使后期，低血回一口也就6-7点，不如一个白板天赋一口奶11加坚韧还能重复用。 5.商店都是抽奖，导致收益普遍不高，最高收益就是连战+坐火升级技能。 打起来就有点累+无聊了。 希望制作组可以参考下， 穿越方尖碑：升级不同流派可以有比较大的变化，商店可以在多个物品中选择购买。等等类似的设定 重置一部分没什么存在感的技能 给传说装备多加点特殊效果，强不强不一定，但是要有独特玩法 总之还是蛮有潜力的，加油
蛮无聊的，职业不多，同类职业之间差异化不明显，英雄成长也不明显，感觉就不能让玩家爽起来，好不容易等到后期要大杀四方的时候，游戏就结束了。技能变化也不行，技能升级也就是数值变化。剧情、美工、UI界面等更不用说了，还有很大的提升 空间。总而言之，不值这个价。

thought i found a hiddern gem at first played to valor 6 so far on hardest difficulty but what ruins it for me is : - during my turn every enemy always counter attacks at least once or twice - they move when u hit them - when hero A attacks an enemy, that enemy runs and counter attacks Hero B ? wtf ?? very frustrating when 8 enemies counter hit you 16 times, then attack you twice each, when its their turn. it just make no sense to me and ruins the fun. you cant propperly plan your turn.

Do you like RPGs with great, satisfyingly fun battle systems? Would you like that battle system to have hundreds of different skills for your characters to use? Want to fight with hundreds of different items? And maybe you'd like a game you pay for to have lots of gameplay to enjoy, like you could see yourself playing it for 100 hours or more? Then you should buy this game immediately. It is easily the best game I've ever seen with less than 200 reviews. Go full price, just straight up buy the game, no questions asked, it's worth it. The only thing truly wrong with this game is that I want more of it. Modding capability, more chapters per run, more characters to play, etc. And when you love this game after playing it (which anyone appreciating an intelligent combat-focused RPG would) you should leave a review too. This game is an absolute achievement, and more people need to know about it.

This game is played in a series of runs, each run being 3 chapters that culminate in a final boss fight. It strongly channels Slay the Spire without cards...only someone seems to have said, "Let's take Slay the Spire and put it into a tactical RPG combat system." Well, it worked. This is a fresh and enjoyable take on both genres and if you enjoy either, I recommend giving this game a try (with a caveat). Your party of 4 adventurers will face 15 encounters in each chapter that culminate in a boss fight. You get to choose what type of encounter you will face (fight, merchant, event, camp), but don't know the specifics until the encounter begins. Resolving the encounter usually means a reward that feels meaningful. Whether its selecting loot, leveling your team, or simply deciding whether to risk spending money on an unknown piece of equipment, each choice you make is an impactful tradeoff that determines how your team will develop. My only grudge with this game so far, is that pacing for unlocked new characters is too slow. So far, I've beaten the game twice and I haven't unlocked a single new character yet? I'd much prefer if the game unlocked at least 1 new character after each successful run...otherwise I will lose interest long before actually unlocking these new characters. The "StS but encounters are tactical battles" is implemented perfectly competently here, but what really makes Valor of Man stand out are the unique mechanics that those tactical battles revolve around. In addition to the actions that they take on their turns, enemies have reactions that are triggered every time that they're the primary target of a player character's attack. This system is quite intricate and takes some getting used to (toggle the bestiary tab on and *read* enemy's abilities when you first encounter them), but it's a very compelling riff on the standard some-flavor-of-initiative-based turn ordering systems. The second major twist is that player characters can be eliminated from combat either when their HP reaches 0 *or* when their secondary resource ("courage") reaches 0. This resource can be reduced by enemies, but is more frequently reduced as a cost associated with the use of more powerful player abilities. This cost often only triggers some percentage of the time that a given ability is used, which speaks to my only substantive complaint about game mechanics to this point - much of the variance revolves around dodging low rolls on non-deterministic courage loss and/or enemy reaction triggers, and it seems like there might be a more elegant solution here than x% chance of outcome y (Larger courage pools with deterministic costs? Removing fail chance from enemy reactions and toning them down accordingly?). Overall Valor of Man is worth trying to see if the combat system clicks with you, and if the game attracts enough attention to continue development I would not be at all surprised to see some of the novel mechanics here show up in other tactical combat contexts.
